pick.headline: Crowds topple Dzerzhinskiy's statue outside KGB headquarters
pick.fbis: The Soviet Union Daily Report of August 23, 1991, carried Russian Television on crowds flooding Dzerzhinskiy Square and besieging the CPSU Central Committee, and Moscow INTERFAX reporting that the Dzerzhinskiy statue had been dismantled at 23:30 on the city's decision.

evidence.title: FBIS Daily Report: Soviet Union, No. 164, 23 August 1991
evidence.snippet: …cow. Some of them FBIS-SOV-91-164 23 August 1991 stated previously their determination to storm the building. Some time before the building of the CPSU Central Committee was blockaded, the demonstrators had also flooded Dzerzhinskiy Square near the KGB building. alternates.headline: KGB chief Kryuchkov arrested with the coup plotters
alternates.fbis: The Soviet Union Daily Report of August 22, 1991, carried Radio Mayak relaying Reuters on the arrests of Yanayev, Yazov, Kryuchkov, Tizyakov and Pugo, Radio Moscow announcing Kryuchkov's arrest, and TASS reporting Pugo's suicide as officials came to detain him.

evidence.snippet: …Results of Failure Arrests Reported LD2208065891 Moscow All-Union Radio Mayak Network in Russian 0630 GMT 22 Aug 91 [Text] The REUTER agency, quoting Stankevich’s state- ment, has reported the arrest of Yanayev, Yazov. Kryuchkov, Tizyakov, and Pugo.
